checks_run.actual:
Shard 1: 107 files, 1059 passed. Shard 2: 107 files, 975 passed, 1 skipped, 1 todo, exit 0. Shard 3: 107 files, 1303 passed.

Shard 4, attempt 1: 46 suites failed on 'ENOSPC: no space left on device' and 'could not extend file ... No space left on device' while migrating (the shared disk). The log is kept as attempt1-enospc.

Shard 4, re-run: 106 files, 938 passed, 1 failed, exit 1. The failure is search/index-feed.test.ts 'an archive sets is_archived' (is_archived false right after one runIndexFeed). By design (ADR-0057 §2), the feed treats an audit event as settled only when it is older than pg_snapshot_xmin(pg_current_snapshot()), which is cluster-wide (apps/worker/src/handlers/search.ts:99-103 and :160-170). An open transaction in another test database on the same disposable cluster can therefore defer the archive event to the next feed run. The product then retries and reports the index as behind (stale), so this is not lost data. The test assumes immediate settlement, which breaks under parallel load. Run alone, the file passes 17/17 (log 33). I judge it a load-sensitive test, not a product defect.

(1) Audit trail. A TL who holds audit read and gets 404 on B02 still learns B02's id as the recordId of B02's own redacted events (log 41: 'the unfiltered trail names the hidden benefit as a recordId: true'). Literally, this is the disclosure D-219's trigger names. (2) Grant register recordId is shown only to holders of sensitive_record.read, who administer grants by id: no new reader. (3) The phase-step evidence remove response echoes the id the writer sent: no new disclosure. The sweep's id allowances used are exactly listAuditEvents, listTransformationAudit, listSensitiveGrants and getSensitiveGrant.

Observation: the audit `reason` text is not scanned for uuids. It is free text written by the actor, and I found no product path that writes an id into it.

checks_run.procedure: Judge whether reading the stored column under the advisory lock and FOR UPDATE keeps the 0101 guard's intent (D-216 question).
checks_run.command: git diff 031945d8..70f05ed4 -- apps/worker apps/api/src/modules/operations (empty); integration concurrent-exception-recurrence.test.ts
checks_run.environment: Code reading; the integration runs
checks_run.expected: No lost or double-counted occurrence; the guard never fires on a legitimate raise.
checks_run.actual: Sound; unchanged since round 6, where I judged it with mutants (the round-7 diff touches neither apps/worker nor operations). Both raisers take pg_advisory_xact_lock(operationalExceptionUpsert, hashtext(key)) and then SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, so in READ COMMITTED they read the latest committed count and version. The UPDATE is guarded by version = current.version with executeTakeFirstOrThrow. greatest(now(), last_occurred_at) is computed in SQL at microsecond precision, so the 0101 guard (NEW < OLD) never fires, and the count goes up by 1 per raise under the lock. A concurrent resolve makes the re-check fail, and a new row opens (ADR-0053). The BE-Z8 test passes 7/7 in both locales.
